title: [Power Display] Monitor "P275MV PLUS" is duplicated in the application menu and fails to detect correctly until system reboot
summary: P275MV PLUS can disappear after refresh or wake and has duplicate persisted identities; a recent comment says a function helped, but does not identify the setting or establish a complete fix.

status.label: Design ready with hardware validation
status.detail: The diagnostic and source evidence support degraded discovery and conservative identity handling, while the latest positive observation needs a precise setting and current-main confirmation.

next_action.label: Approve Power Display degraded-discovery design
next_action.reason: The design addresses the observed DDC failure and duplicate identity path, with a targeted request for the newly reported workaround details.

judgment.rationale: The report and diagnostic archive identify a monitor that remains in the active display inventory but is omitted after DDC capability acquisition fails, while persisted entries can retain more than one identity. The latest comment says a function improved detection, but it does not name the function or show that duplicate handling and normal-mode discovery are fixed, so the design remains actionable with a focused validation gap.
evidence: The issue reports duplicate P275MV PLUS entries and disappearance from the Power Display menu until a system restart.
The report includes screenshots and a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP.
The prior diagnostic investigation recorded the same EdidId with different DevicePath segments and repeated empty DDC capability responses for an active display.
The latest public comment reports that a function helped and monitoring is now always detected, but does not identify the function or its version.
Current DdcCiController.DiscoverFromHandleAsync discards a physical monitor when FetchCapabilitiesWithFallbackAsync returns no capabilities.
Current MonitorSettingsRebuilder preserves missing entries by age but does not coalesce stale same-monitor identities with changed DevicePath values.
Existing history includes wake rescan, stable IDs, persisted VCP fallback, and maximum-compatibility probing, but no single change is confirmed to cover this issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the conservative degraded-discovery and identity-reconciliation design, then confirm the newly reported function and reproduce the wake/capability failure on current main hardware.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked PowerToys fix or concrete implementation is confirmed. Existing wake and compatibility work improves adjacent paths but does not prove that a DisplayConfig-present monitor remains visible after DDC capability failure or that stale duplicate identities are removed.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep DDC-flaky displays visible and coalesce only stale duplicate identities
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Normal discovery treats missing DDC capabilities as evidence that a physical monitor should be dropped even when DisplayConfig still reports it. Persisted settings can then retain older DevicePath variants for the same panel, producing duplicate rows. The recent workaround observation may reduce the failure frequency but does not identify a complete fix.
plan: Retain a physical monitor as degraded when DisplayConfig and physical-handle evidence are valid and recent known-good VCP evidence exists, while keeping unsupported controls disabled.
Retry live discovery on refresh or wake and clear degraded state only after a successful live capability read.
Reconcile persisted identities conservatively by preferring a currently discovered identity and coalescing only stale same-EdidId/name entries.
Validate the reported workaround setting and hardware behavior before broadening deduplication rules.
verification: An empty live capability response for an active P275MV PLUS leaves one degraded row visible instead of removing it.
A later successful refresh replaces degraded evidence with live capabilities.
One current identity plus stale same-EdidId/name entries results in one persisted row.
Two simultaneously discovered identical monitors remain separate.
The setting or function named by the latest commenter is tested on current main and its effect is recorded.

confidence.rationale: The omission path and identity-retention behavior are directly supported by the report, diagnostics, source, and history. Confidence remains yellow because the hardware-specific wake behavior and the newly reported successful function need exact identification and current-main validation.

issue_context.summary: Power Display loses or duplicates a P275MV PLUS around DDC capability failures and changing monitor identities; a recent comment reports improvement without enough detail to close the design question.

The issue includes two screenshots and a diagnostic ZIP attachment.
The original report says the monitor disappears from the menu and returns after a computer restart.
A later observation says the monitor can remain missing after standby and wake.
The prior diagnostic evidence recorded an active display with repeated empty DDC capability responses and duplicate same-EdidId identities with different DevicePath segments.

There is no assignee, linked fix, or confirmed duplicate relationship in the live issue.
inferences: DisplayConfig presence should determine whether a monitor row exists, while DDC capability readiness should determine which controls are enabled.
A currently discovered identity should take precedence over stale persisted identities for the same EdidId and normalized name.
The reported function may be an existing compatibility or rescan path, but that is not confirmed from the public comment.
issue_context.analysis: The new positive observation is material but underspecified. It should not be ignored, yet it does not disprove the source and diagnostic path or establish that the issue is handled in normal mode. The proposed design therefore preserves the existing evidence, adds a conservative degraded state, and asks only for the setting/function identity and a current-main wake trace needed to validate whether an existing path already covers the failure.

design.root_cause: Normal Power Display discovery drops a physical monitor when DDC capability acquisition returns no usable capabilities, despite QueryDisplayConfig and the physical handle identifying an active display. Persisted monitor settings can retain older DevicePath variants, so a single panel can appear more than once. The current source and diagnostics support this mechanism; the latest workaround comment may indicate an adjacent mitigation but does not identify it.
evidence: [Observed] The report shows a P275MV PLUS disappearing from the Power Display menu and duplicate-looking entries.
[Observed] A later comment says the monitor can remain absent after standby and wake.
[Observed] The diagnostic archive previously showed an active display with repeated empty DDC capability responses and same-EdidId identity variants.
[Observed] DiscoverFromHandleAsync releases and discards a physical monitor when evidence.Capabilities is null.
[Observed] MonitorSettingsRebuilder only matches exact stable IDs and age-retains unmatched persisted entries.
[Observed] Recent history added wake rescans and persisted VCP fallback, but the normal drop condition remains in the current source.
[Inferred] Separating monitor existence from control capability and coalescing only stale identities addresses both symptoms without inventing support.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: After retries and optional maximum-compatibility probing, a null capability result causes DiscoverFromHandleAsync to release the physical handle and omit the monitor.
implementation_steps.change: When the physical handle and DisplayConfig identity are valid, use recent exact-monitor known-good VCP evidence to construct a degraded monitor. Preserve the existing discard behavior when no positive evidence exists or the handle is invalid. Mark degraded state separately so controls remain guarded.
edge_cases: Never synthesize support from a generic model name alone.
Guard all writes when the monitor is degraded and require live success to clear the flag.
Keep cancellation and invalid-handle outcomes distinct from a recoverable capability failure.
Ensure abandoned handles are still destroyed on every null/exception path.
tests: Known-good evidence plus empty live capabilities yields a degraded monitor.
Empty live capabilities without known-good evidence preserves the existing omission behavior.
Invalid physical handle still releases the handle and does not create a monitor.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Persisted entries are deduplicated only by exact stable ID; stale DevicePath variants for one physical monitor can survive as separate recent entries.
implementation_steps.change: After emitting current monitors, coalesce only unmatched stale entries that share a normalized EdidId and normalized friendly name with a current identity. Prefer the current identity and newest settings, preserve user flags, and leave two currently discovered identical monitors separate.
edge_cases: Do not merge two simultaneous current identities.
Do not merge entries when EdidId or normalized name is missing.
Preserve hidden/user-configured flags conservatively when choosing the retained record.
Use MonitorIdComparer for exact ID equality and a separately documented normalized identity key for stale reconciliation.
tests: One current identity plus one stale same-EdidId/name entry yields one row and preserves user flags.
Two current identical monitors remain two rows.
Different EdidIds or names remain separate.
Old unrelated entries continue to expire by the existing retention rule.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The UI rebuilds its list from returned monitors and removes any monitor that discovery omitted; controls do not distinguish degraded capability state.
implementation_steps.change: Retain degraded monitor rows returned by the discovery layer, show an unavailable-controls state, and clear that state only when a subsequent live discovery succeeds. Keep refresh and wake paths on the same state transition.
edge_cases: Do not expose or batch-write unsupported controls.
Ensure HasMonitors and empty-state properties reflect retained degraded rows.
Avoid replacing a healthy row with degraded state when a newer successful discovery exists.
tests: The view model retains a degraded row and disables unsupported controls.
A live recovery clears the degraded state after refresh.
Hidden monitor filtering and empty-state properties remain correct.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Existing tests cover retry/cache gates and exact ID retention but not degraded visible rows or stale same-monitor identity coalescing.
implementation_steps.change: Add deterministic tests for the new evidence and identity policies, then run the narrowest existing Power Display test and build commands.
edge_cases: Tests must not call real DDC hardware.
Cover a successful recovery after a degraded pass.
tests: Run PowerDisplay.Lib.UnitTests with filters for DdcCiController and MonitorSettingsRebuilder.

verify: Confirm the exact function/setting and build named by the latest public commenter.
On current main, reproduce standby/wake or inject an empty DDC capability response while QueryDisplayConfig still reports the P275MV PLUS.
With the fix, verify one degraded monitor row remains visible and unsupported controls are disabled.
Recover DDC and refresh; verify live capabilities replace degraded state.
Verify one current identity plus stale DevicePath variants does not recreate duplicate rows, while two simultaneous identical monitors remain distinct.
Run the focused PowerDisplay.Lib.UnitTests and x64 Release build.
risks: Cached VCP evidence can become stale; degraded controls must remain read/write guarded until live success.
Conservative identity matching can still merge two physical identical monitors if current-versus-stale classification is wrong; never group two current identities.
Retaining a degraded row changes the empty-state UX but is safer than hiding an active display.
Hardware-specific wake timing may require a bounded retry or wake rescan in addition to the degraded fallback.
alternatives: Only increasing DDC retries does not address a persistent empty capability response or stale duplicate identities.
Making maximum-compatibility mode the only solution leaves normal mode vulnerable and depends on an unconfirmed workaround.
Deduplicating every same-model entry risks merging two physically connected identical monitors; current-discovery exclusion is required.
A UI-only placeholder would show the monitor without a safe evidence source for its controls.
